events.note: Faint CME observed to the N in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, not in STEREO A COR2. cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.

events.note: Faint CME first seen to the West by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-09-30T11:36Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. This event is not clearly seen in STEREO A COR2 as it is likely obscured by the occulting disk. The source of this CME is a small eruption from the vicinity of former AR 14543 (S08W112) seen beginning at approx. 2026-09-30T10:55Z in STEREO A EUVI 195.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1.

events.note: Faint CME observed to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. May be observed to the NE in STEREO A COR2, but difficult to reliably resolve in white light imagery. The source is likely far-sided, only observed as weak field line movement over the NE limb in SDO AIA 171 starting as early as 2026-10-01T00:25Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: StereoCAT SOHO LASCO C2 plane-of-sky due to the uncertain far-sided source. Half width measuring 7-8 degrees.
Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. CME is thin (HW slightly <10 degrees) and somewhat deflected, but still tracks a decent fit between the coronagraphs.

events.note: Faint CME observed to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The source is far-sided, approximately ~N12W120, as observed in STEREO A EUVI 195/304 as brightening starting around 2026-10-01T02:35Z. Also observed in SDO AIA 171/193/304 as filament ejecta and field line movement beyond the NW limb starting around 2026-10-01T02:36Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 StereoCAT triangulation. Due to STEREO A COR2 white light image quality and the faint CME front, it is difficult to track, and the parameters may vary somewhat.

events.note: CME faintly visible to the NE in STEREO A COR2 and the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. Post-eruption arcades are also visible, and best seen after a data gap in STEREO A EUV 195 imagery. The data gap is from 2026-10-01T14:35Z to 2026-10-02T00:55Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1 in SWPC_CAT as well as the potential source location.

events.note: Faint CME seen to the NNE in GOES CCOR-1 and SOHO LASCO C2/C3. The CME is also possibly faintly visible in STEREO A COR2 imagery to the NE. The potential source may be a filament liftoff faintly seen in SDO AIA 304 imagery starting at 2026-10-01T22:01Z around N45E05. No other candidate source eruptions are seen in available EUV imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the potential source location as well as the best fit between STEREO A COR2, SOHO LASCO C3, and GOES CCOR-1 imagery in SWPC_CAT.

events.note: CME visible to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. The CME overlaps in the field of view with the CME first seen in STEREO A COR2 at 2026-10-02T00:53Z.  The CME may potentially be faintly seen to the NNE in STEREO A COR2. The potential source may be AR 14535, located around N11W75, with a small region of brightening and moving field lines best seen in SDO AIA 193 imagery starting at 2026-10-02T05:52Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery in SWPC_CAT as well as potential source location.

events.note: Very faint CME/outflow with an unclear leading edge seen to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. This CME is not seen in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap. No source was found in EUV imagery for this outflow.

cmeAnalyses.note: A plane-of-sky measurement was made using a longitude of -90 degrees due to unclear (possibly far-sided) source and absence of STEREO A imagery due to data gap.

events.note: Faint narrow CME with an anvil-like front seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and fully covered by a large data gap in STEREO A COR2. Its source is likely the notable prominence off/behind the east limb that is best seen in SDO AIA 304/171 and GOES SUVI 304/284. In SUVI it this filament is seen deflecting northwardly.

cmeAnalyses.note: The source of this event is a notable filament eruption seen from behind the east limb in SDO AIA 304/171 and GOES SUVI 304/284, making the source location not clear (likely somewhat behind the east limb). The event is covered by an extensive data gap in STEREO A COR2 coronagraph. Therefore only plane-of-sky analysis is possible.

events.note: This CME is visible to the east in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The source is likely far-sided as there are no source signatures on the Earth-facing disk around the time of this event.

cmeAnalyses.note: A plane-of-sky measurement was made using a longitude of -90 degrees due to the far-sided and therefore unknown source location.

events.note: Extremely faint CME/outflow with an unclear leading edge seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 and in early C3 and GOES CCOR-1 running difference imagery. This CME is not seen in STEREO A COR2 due to a  data gap. No clear source was found in EUV imagery for this outflow.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky using longitude of E90 due to data gap covering this faint event in STEREO A COR2 and absence of clear source.

events.note: Faint CME observed to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2, poorly observed in LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1, and not in STEREO A COR2; mostly overlapped with following CME: 2026-10-04T07:36Z. The source is likely the first of two paired B-class flares and respective field line movement from AR 14546; this front associated with the B3.2 class flare peaking at 2026-10-04T06:19Z and field line movement in SDO AIA 171.

cmeAnalyses.note: SOHO LASCO C2 only 3D analysis using observed source longitude of W62, as such the parameters may slightly vary.

events.note: Faint CME observed to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2, poorly observed in LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1, and not in STEREO A COR2;  mostly overlapped with preceeding CME: 2026-10-04T07:24Z. The source is likely the second of two paired B-class flares and respective field line movement from AR 14546; this front associated with the B9.3 class flare peaking at 2026-10-04T06:30Z and broad field line movement/dimming in SDO AIA 171/193.

cmeAnalyses.note: SOHO LASCO C2 only 3D analysis using observed source longitude of W62, as such the parameters may slightly vary.

events.note: Filament eruption observed to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2. In real-time the event is slow and not yet observed in other coronagraphs, but will likely be partially obscured by the LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 pylons. The source is a far-sided filament eruption over the SE limb observed in SDO AIA 171/193/304, and GOES SUVI 304, starting around 2026-10-04T15:30Z as filament ejecta and field line movement. It is unclear how far-sided the source is, but being near the limb it is likely within E90-E120.

cmeAnalyses.note: SOHO LASCO C2 only plane-of-sky as the only observing coronagraph so far, and unknown far-sided longitude of the source.

events.note: Faint CME observed to the W in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, not observed in STEREO A COR2. The source is AR 14546 starting around 2026-10-05T00:33Z, with brightening and field line movement in SDO AIA 171/193, and some dimming in SDO AIA 193, centered around S21W71.

cmeAnalyses.note: SOHO LASCO C3 only 3D analysis using the source W71, as such the parameters may vary. There is a concurrent SW feature in COR2A that does not triangulate to this SOHO LASCO feature and is ruled a separate event, so SOHO-only is used here.

events.note: Wide CME observed to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, and to the NW in STEREO A COR2. The source is a far-sided filament eruption over the NE limb, observed in SDO AIA 171/193/304 as field line movement, EUV wave, and filament ejecta starting around 2026-10-05T07:18Z, although these features are better observed in the wider field-of-view in GOES SUVI 171/193/284/304. Also observed weakly in STEREO A EUVI over its NW limb starting in EUVI 304 as filament ejecta around 2026-10-05T06:45Z and in EUVI 195 as field line movement around 2026-10-05T07:25Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. This analysis encompasses the entire observed front as the bulk leading edge with no discernable shock, taking note of the brighter inner core.

events.note: Faint CME observed to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The source is in the vicinity of AR 14548 (S11E46), as a weak eruption centered around S17E60 starting around 2026-10-05T08:55Z observed in SDO AIA 171/193 as filament brightening and field line movement without the small filament seen cleanly lifting off the disk.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2, the front is quite faint but still trackable in early frames.

events.note: This CME is visible to the northwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely related to a far-sided filament eruption which begins to lift-off around 2026-10-05T19:00Z as seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304 and GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

events.note: This CME is visible to the west/southwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. This event is not seen in STEREO A COR2 imagery likely due to a data gap from 2026-10-05T14:38Z to 2026-10-06T01:23Z. The source is a small eruption visible from Active Region 14546 (S19W88) as seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304 and GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304 imagery starting around 2026-10-05T23:15Z. A subsequent opening of field lines visible over the southwest limb in SDO AIA 171/193 and GOES SUVI 171/195/284 imagery at this time as well.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measured longitude based on the on-disk source location.

events.note: Full halo CME in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, first seen to the NE in STEREO A COR2 (shock fully to the E, wide). The source is AR 14549, associated with an M1.4 flare (N10E12) peaking at 2026-10-06T06:10Z, observed in SDO AIA 131. Also observed as an EUV wave, field line movement, brightening, filament ejecta, and small post-eruptive arcade in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304. Additionally observed on the NE limb of STEREO A EUVI 195 as field line movement and EUV wave, and EUVI 304 as filament ejecta.

cmeAnalyses.note: Bulk leading edge triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2, noting the slightly distorted shape of the bright LE affecting analysis of the width. This analysis is initially preliminary, but may stand as final LE.

Shock triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2, noting the asymmetric shape of the shock especially in the LASCO C2/C3 field-of-view. This analysis is initially preliminary, but may stand as final SH.

events.note: CME observed to the NE in STEREO A COR2, also faintly observed to the N in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. The source is AR 14549, associated with an M1.8 class flare (N08E07) peaking at 2026-10-06T08:05Z, observed in SDO AIA 131. Also observed as field line movement, EUV wave, dimming, and brightening in SDO AIA 171/193 starting around 2026-10-06T07:52Z, with brightening and filament ejecta in SDO AIA 304. Also observed well in STEREO A EUVI 195/304 starting around 2026-10-06T08:05Z as field line movement and filament ejecta on the NE limb, with some northward deflection.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation betweeen SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. The CME front is much more faint in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, so the width in COR2 is used primarily.

events.note: Faint CME first seen to the NNE by STEREO A COR2 beginning at 2026-10-06T13:08Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.

events.note: CME first seen to the NE in STEREO A COR2 starting at 2026-10-07T13:53Z. So far it is only visible in COR2A. The source of this CME is a C7.9 class flare from AR 14549 (N10W04) peaking at 2026-10-07T13:17Z best seen in SDO AIA 171. Some dimming and an EUVI wave associated with the eruption can be seen in SDO AIA 193. Some deflection is evident in the measurement of this CME, likely due to it close proximity to a coronal hole to the SE of AR 14549.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit among SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2.

events.note: CME faintly seen to the east in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. The CME may potentially be visible to the west in STEREO A COR2. Some ejecta of material can also be seen beyond the east limb in GOES SUVI 304 as well.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery in SWPC_CAT. Due to the CME's faintness, this CME measurement is more approximate than usual.

events.note: CME visible to the west in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 as well as possibly faintly to the east in STEREO A COR2. This CME overlaps in the field of view with the CME first seen in STEREO A COR2 at 2026-10-08T16:53Z. The potential source is a filament eruption centered around N05W25 as best seen in SDO AIA 193/304 imagery. The eruption is best seen as dimming starting at 2026-10-08T09:21Z in SDO AIA 193. The filament liftoff can be best seen from the point of view of STEREO A EUV 195/304, in the NE quadrant from the point of view of STEREO A.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on potential source location as well as best fit between SOHO LASCO C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. There were two measurable frames of STEREO A COR2 imagery available for this measurement. There may be some deflection of the CME.

events.note: CME visible to the NE in STEREO A COR2 and the NW in GOES CCOR-1. There was a real-time data gap in SOHO LASCO imagery at the start of the CME, but this backfilled with additional imagery. The source for this CME is an M6.7 class flare from AR 14549 (N12W20) which peaked at 2026-10-08T15:48Z. The flare is best seen in SDO AIA 131. The accompanying EUV wave which spans the entire NW quadrant of the Earth-facing disk is best seen in SDO AIA 193. The eruption is also visible in STEREO A EUV 195/304 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Preliminary measurement of the leading edge based on the best fit between GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2 imagery in SWPC_CAT.
Preliminary shock measurement using the best fit between GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2 imagery in SWPC_CAT.
Updated measurement of the leading edge of the CME based on the source location as well as the best fit between SOHO LASCO C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

events.note: Faint CME observed to the E only in STEREO A COR2 Science Data, as a real-time gap in STEREO A COR2 beacon data spanning 2026-10-08T18:53Z to 2026-10-09T17:53Z obscured real-time observations of this CME. CME leading edge not observed in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 or GOES CCOR-1. Partial overlap with CMEs 2026-10-08T16:24Z and CME 2026-10-08T16:53Z. The source is an on-disk filament eruption in the vicinity of AR 14548, starting around 2026-10-08T17:13Z, with the filament spanning a curved arc from S08E15 to S21E24 to S15E05 before liftoff in SDO AIA 304. Eruption observed as filament ejecta, brightening, and double-ribbon flare in SDO AIA 304, and as field line movement, dimming, and brightening/post-eruptive arcades in SDO AIA 171/193/211.

cmeAnalyses.note: 3D STEREO A COR2 Science Data only analysis, fitting to the approximate center of the eruptive source ~S16E13 and finding northward deflection. Science data imagery is used due to a real-time STEREO A COR2 beacon data gap spanning 2026-10-08T18:53Z to 2026-10-09T17:53Z, and no leading edge observations in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1.

events.note: CME visible to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, directly following CME: 2026-10-08T16:53Z in the field of view. The CME is not visible in STEREO A COR2, and a data gap starts at 2026-10-08T18:53Z. The potential source is unclear, with several potential source candidates on the disk. The most likely candidate is a possible eruption from AR 14547 (N15W85) seen starting around 2026-10-08T16:19Z as dimming and moving field lines. The eruption is also faintly visible from the point of view of STEREO A EUV 195 imagery. Another candidate source is a filament eruption starting around 2026-10-08T18:09Z centered around S15E10 as seen in SDO AIA 193/304, but this is not a likely source candidate due to the location of the eruption. This eruption's proximity to a coronal hole may result in some deflection of the eruption. The third possible eruption candidate is activity from AR 14549 (N10W25), but it is not clear if this is a separate eruption from the one that produced CME: 2026-10-08T16:53Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the potential source location. STEREO A COR2 was not available for triangulation of this measurement.

events.note: CME faintly seen to the east in GOES CCOR-1 imagery. There is a data gap in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery starting at 2026-10-09T00:48Z and a data gap starting in STEREO A COR2 at 2026-10-09T00:53Z. The source is likely beyond the E limb as seen in available EUV imagery, as slow moving field lines are visible on the E limb in SDO AIA 193 and GOES SUVI 284 imagery starting as early as 2026-10-08T18:30Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane of sky measurement using GOES CCOR-1 running difference imagery in SWPC_CAT.

events.note: CME seen to the NW in GOES CCOR-1 imagery. There is a data gap in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 at the time of this CME. The potential source is unclear, but is likely an eruption from AR 14547 (approximately N15W90) starting around 2026-10-09T06:30Z, best seen as moving/opening field lines in SDO AIA 193 and GOES SUVI 284 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on source location using GOES CCOR-1 imagery.

events.note: CME visible to the NNW in GOES CCOR-1 imagery. There is no SOHO LASCO C2/C3 or STEREO A COR2 data available during this time, with a data gap in SOHO imagery starting at 2026-10-09T00:48Z and no STEREO A COR2 data available since 2026-10-09T01:09Z. The source for this CME is not found in available EUV imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane of sky measurement using GOES CCOR-1 running difference imagery in SWPC_CAT.

events.note: Faint CME with a loop front seen to the NW in the early SOHO LASCO C2 imagery, also seen faintly in C3 and GOES CCOR-1. It is fully covered by long data gap in STEREO A COR2 coronagraph. The source is the occulted (or on-limb) M1.3 flare likely from Active Region 14547 (N15W94), now decayed to a plage, which had just rotated off the visible disk before the flare. Other coronal signatures include a small ejecta seen in SDO AIA 304 at the time of the flare and movement/opening of field lines seen to the NW behind the limb in SDO AIA 171/193 and GOES SUVI 304/284.

cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis based on the location of the source (the M1.3 flare from Active Region 14547 (N15W94) which had just rotated off the visible disk before the flare) and on imagery from SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 The CME is fully covered by long data gap in STEREO A COR2 coronagraph, so this analysis is not confirmed by STEREO A.

events.note: CME observed to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The source is former AR 14547 (~N15W105) as directly observed by STEREO A around the west limb from SDO. Observed across SDO AIA 131/171/193/211/304 as field line movement and EUV wave, and brightening, starting around 2026-10-10T07:51Z, partially obscured by a rare transit of the moon across the SDO AIA field-of-view. Also seen in STEREO A EUVI 195/304 as brightening, dimming, and field line movement starting around 2026-10-10T07:55Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

events.note: Very minor, faint, and narrow CME seen to the NE in STEREO A COR2 coronagraph in early timestamps. This is possibly the same faint narrow CME that is also seen at the time NE in SOHO LASCO C2 for a few early timestamps and not seen in C3 or GOES C3. No source has been found  in EUV imagery for this event.

cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis based on the fit of the narrow NE fronts in STEREO A COR2 and SOHO LASCO C2.

events.note: CME observed to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, with a full halo shock. Not yet observed in STEREO A COR2 white light imagery in real-time. The source is AR 14549, associated with an M6.4 flare peaking at 2026-10-10T15:10Z observed in SDO AIA 131. Also observed starting around 2026-10-10T15:04Z as field line movement and very large EUV wave, some dimming, and brightening/post eruptive arcades in SDO AIA 131/171/193/211/304.

cmeAnalyses.note: Bulk measurement. SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 fit using W54 as the flare longitude, given no available STEREO A COR2 to triangulate with.

This analyzed longitude is significantly far from the eruptive source around W54 degrees, but the entire shock front does not otherwise fit within the swpc_cat tool at more western longitudes.

events.note: Minor faint, narrow CME/outflow seen to the west in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and covered by the data gap in STEREO A. No clear source has been found for this CME.

cmeAnalyses.note: This minor CME is not seen in STEREO A COR2 because of the data gap in STEREO. No source has been found for this CME. Only plane-of-sky analysis is possible for this CME.

events.note: Outflow first seen to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2 starting around 2026-10-11T09:12Z. This feature is much easier to see later in its propagation into SOHO LASCO C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The source is most likely outflow following CME: 2026-10-10T16:15Z but may be related to field line movement seen near the NW limb in SDO AIA 193 starting as early as 2026-10-11T05:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit among SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2.

events.note: This CME is visible to the east in GOES CCOR-1 and SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery. This event is seen in STEREO A COR2, directed towards the east, after it has exceeded the field of view due to a data gap from 2026-10-11T17:38Z to 2026-10-12T01:53Z. The source is a filament eruption spanning S30E30 to S10E05 which begins to lift off around 2026-10-11T22:30Z as seen in SDO 131/171/193/304 and GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304 imagery. Dimming is visible in SDO AIA 193 and GOES SUVI 195 imagery, with post eruptive arcades visible starting around 2026-10-11T23:40Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the approximate source location. Although this leading edge for this event is outside of the STEREO A COR2 field of view, this imagery was used as a guide to find the best fitting parameters between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

events.note: This CME is visible to the southwest in GOES CCOR-1 and SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery. This event is not seen in STEREO A COR2 in real-time due to a data gap starting at 2026-10-11T17:38Z. The source may be related to dimming centered near S20E30 starting around 2026-10-11T22:00Z as seen in SDO AIA 193 and GOES SUVI 195 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measured longitude based on the source location. Due to a data gap in STEREO A COR2 imagery, a triangulated measurement was not available and the measured parameters may vary slightly as a result.

events.note: This CME is visible to the east in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. For this leading edge, the eruptive source is likely field line movement/brightening in SDO AIA 171/193, and on-disk brightening in SDO AIA 304 and STEREO A EUVI 304, starting around 2026-10-26T08:31Z and centered around S09W72. This eruption is also associated with a C1.9 flare peaking at 2026-10-26T08:38Z, observed in SDO AIA 131.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.
